name: comparator-regeneration
description: Decision (regeneration) time of the full comparator over PVT at 0.5 LSB / 100 mV / 0.1 mV input overdrive, measured on a strobe that must flip a latch holding the opposite answer; the extracted regeneration time constant and metastability margin; the block's total static current and its dynamic energy per decision.
claim: README.md#target-specification -- sample rate 1 MS/s (2 MS/s stretch) and power < 1 mW (< 500 uW stretch). The comparator must complete a decision inside the 31.25 ns decide phase of the 62.5 ns bit cycle spec/prior-art-survey.md S1.4 allocates (15.625 ns at the 2 MS/s stretch) at every PVT corner, and spec/comparator-budget-memo.md S6 states the metastability margin this record measures.
analyses: meas tran td_a trig v(clkn) val=0.5 rise=2 targ v(dan) val=0.5 rise=1
meas tran td_d trig v(clkn) val=0.5 rise=2 targ v(ddn) val=0.5 rise=1
meas tran td_e trig v(clkn) val=0.5 rise=2 targ v(den) val=0.5 rise=1
meas tran va_mid find v(dan) at=70n
meas tran vd_mid find v(ddn) at=70n
meas tran ve_mid find v(den) at=70n
meas tran va_end find v(dan) at=130n
meas tran vd_end find v(ddn) at=130n
meas tran ve_end find v(den) at=130n
meas tran q_idle integ i(vsupa) from=50n to=70n
meas tran q_act integ i(vsupa) from=72.5n to=135n

td_half_ns.description: THE METASTABILITY CLAIM: clock-to-decision delay at HALF AN LSB of input overdrive -- the smallest differential the converter is ever required to resolve correctly. The ceiling is the 2 MS/s STRETCH decide phase (15.625 ns): at 1 MS/s the bit cycle is 62.5 ns with a 31.25 ns decide phase (spec/prior-art-survey.md S1.4), so passing here passes the ratified rate with 2x more margin. This is measured at every PVT point rather than inferred from the survey's typical-corner 'sub-nanosecond [E4]' estimate, which is the whole point of the criterion. The per-axis floors are the corner-sensitivity guard: regeneration is a gm/C process, so the delay must move with both process and temperature.

td_big_ns.description: Large-signal (100 mV) delay -- the t0 floor of t = t0 + tau*ln(V_logic/(A_v*V_in)). It is the reference point tau is extracted against, and it must itself fit the decide phase; a comparator that cannot resolve 100 mV in time has a reset or a load problem, not a regeneration one.

td_tiny_ns.description: Delay at 0.1 mV (~1/32 LSB), inside the region where a wrong answer is NOT a converter error because the residue is below the quantization floor. Bounded against the 1 MS/s decide phase only: this is a metastability probe, not an accuracy requirement, and the point of measuring it is to show the logarithmic law still holds two decades below the accuracy-critical overdrive rather than collapsing into a stuck latch.

tau_ps.description: Regeneration time constant, EXTRACTED not assumed: tau = (t(0.5 LSB) - t(100 mV)) / ln(100 mV / 1.6113 mV). Every metastability statement in spec/comparator-budget-memo.md S6 -- the minimum resolvable input in a given budget, the error probability per decision, the margin handed to #12 -- is computed from this number, so it is the one that has to be measured over PVT rather than quoted.

margin_ns.description: Slack against the 1 MS/s decide phase (31.25 ns) at half an LSB of overdrive. The floor demands at least half the phase remain unused, which is equivalently the 2 MS/s stretch requirement, stated as a margin so a reader can see how much of the budget the comparator actually spends.

dout_pos_end.description: Decision held at the end of the second bit cycle for a POSITIVE 0.5 LSB input, normalized to the supply.

dout_big_end.description: Decision at +100 mV, held after two cycles.

dout_tiny_end.description: Decision at +0.1 mV, held after two cycles. This is the mismatch-free deck, so even a 1/32 LSB input has a definite correct answer; with mismatch it would not, which is why offset is budgeted separately (sim/comparator-offset-mc/).

e_dec_fj.description: DYNAMIC energy per decision, in femtojoules: charge drawn over one full 62.5 ns bit cycle (the second one, in steady state) minus the charge the same instance draws over a settled clock-low window scaled to the same duration, times the supply. The static preamp term is deliberately excluded here (it is measured in sim/comparator-offset/ as pstat_uw) so the two power terms can be added explicitly in spec/comparator-budget-memo.md S7 rather than double-counted. At 11 decisions per conversion and 1 MS/s the ceiling corresponds to 55 uW of switching power, ~11 % of the < 500 uW stretch budget.

i_static_ua.description: TOTAL static supply current of ONE comparator, measured on its own supply during a SETTLED clock-low window (50-70 ns, after the first decision). It is ~2x the 10 uA bias, not 1x: the 1:1 mirror's diode branch sinks the forced 10 uA from the same supply and the tail branch mirrors another 10 uA, so the block's real static draw is ~20 uA. sim/comparator-offset/'s pstat_uw measures the TAIL branch alone (10 uA, from the load drop); this measurement is the one spec/comparator-budget-memo.md S7 uses for the power row, precisely because it counts the bias branch the other cannot see. Measuring it before the first strobe would instead have caught the SR latch mid-resolution and reported its crowbar current as static bias.

resolve_decades.description: HOW MUCH SMALLER an input the comparator could still resolve inside the 31.25 ns decide phase, in decades below the half-LSB overdrive actually applied: (T_decide - t(0.5 LSB)) / (tau * ln 10). This is the metastability margin stated in a form that does not underflow -- the equivalent minimum resolvable input is 0.5 LSB / 10^(this), which for the measured tau is far below any voltage the PDK's own numerical noise floor could represent, so it is quoted as decades rather than as a fictitious microvolt figure. The floor of 3 decades is the requirement: an input 1000x below half an LSB must still resolve in time, which bounds the metastability error rate in spec/comparator-budget-memo.md S6.

dout_pos_mid.description: THE POLARITY CONTROL, on the SAME instance: before the second strobe the output must still hold the FIRST (negative-input) decision. Together with dout_pos_end this proves the instance decided both ways at the same PVT point -- a latch that was stuck, or one whose SR latch simply started in the answer state, cannot pass both halves.

dout_big_mid.description: The same polarity control at 100 mV.

dout_tiny_mid.description: The same polarity control at 0.1 mV (~1/32 LSB). This is the mismatch-free deck, so even a 1/32 LSB input has a definite correct answer in both directions.

notes: MISMATCH-FREE BY CONSTRUCTION. sw_stat_mismatch is left at the PDK default (0), so every device is nominal. Regeneration time and offset are separable: offset shifts the input at which the decision flips (measured in sim/comparator-offset-mc/), while tau sets how fast a given overdrive resolves. Combining them in one deck would make neither measurable.

TIMING THRESHOLDS ARE SUPPLY-NORMALIZED. Every delay triggers on a node divided by its own supply and crossed at 0.5 (the Bclkn/Bdan/... behavioural sources). A fixed absolute threshold would turn the +/-10 % supply axis into a measurement artefact.

THE ENERGY NUMBER IS SWITCHING ENERGY ONLY, and it is measured on a comparator strobed at the 62.5 ns bit cycle. Converting it to average power requires the real duty (11 decisions per 1 us conversion), which spec/comparator-budget-memo.md S7 does explicitly rather than leaving the reader to assume a 16 MHz continuous strobe.
